• Uma and Deepa live in the same flat letters.
• Kiran lives below Pia.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are branches. All branches are accounts. No accounts is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are not branches.
II. No branches is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: No coins is a branches. Some branches are accounts. All accounts are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are cards.
II. Some cards are branches.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are branches. Some branches are accounts. All accounts are cards.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are cards.
II. No branches is a cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some coins are branches. All branches are accounts. No accounts is a cards.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are accounts.
II. Some branches are cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: W < V > P > Q < S.
Conclusions: I. W < Q   II. W > S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: V < X > U < T = Q.
Conclusions: I. V ≤ X   II. U ≥ T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:

Conclusions: I. U ≥ S   II. U < S.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is definitely true; II is not guaranteed. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
Statements: T > X = S = W > V.
Conclusions: I. W < V   II. S < T.
Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. Trace the chain, retaining strict and equal signs. I is not guaranteed; II is definitely true. The selected conclusion follows across every weak ordering consistent with the statements.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
credit savings secure = to ze lu
credit banking growth = ni lu ka
savings banking access = ka pa to
secure growth access = ze pa ni
credit savings access = lu to pa
What is the code for “banking”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ka. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: credit = lu, savings = to, secure = ze, banking = ka, growth = ni, access = pa.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 46 km east, turns left and walks 40 km, then turns left and walks 16 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 50. Net displacement is 30 km east and 40 km north. By Pythagoras, √(30² + 40²) = 50 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 44 km east, turns left and walks 32 km, then turns left and walks 20 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. Net displacement is 24 km east and 32 km north. By Pythagoras, √(24² + 32²) = 40 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 56 km east, turns left and walks 48 km, then turns left and walks 20 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 60. Net displacement is 36 km east and 48 km north. By Pythagoras, √(36² + 48²) = 60 km.

questions.stem: A is the mother of C. D is the son of C. F is the father of C. How is D related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Grandson. F is a parent of C, and D is C’s son. Hence D is F’s grandchild.

questions.stem: G is the brother of D. D is the mother of A. C is the father of G and D. How is G related to A?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. G is the brother of A’s mother D. Therefore G is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: A is the only daughter of C. C is the father of A. D is the son of A. B is the sister of C. How is C related to D?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of A, and A is D’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 60 candidates, a candidate is 17th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 41. New front rank = 17+3 = 20. Back rank = 60 − 20 + 1 = 41.

questions.stem: In a queue of 52 candidates, a candidate is 18th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 31. New front rank = 18+4 = 22. Back rank = 52 − 22 + 1 = 31.

questions.stem: An item costs ₹1300. It is marked above cost and sold at a 10% discount on marked price, earning 12% profit. Find the marked price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 1617.78. Selling price = 1300 × 112/100. Marked price = selling price ÷ 0.9 = 1617.78.

questions.stem: A can finish a job in 18 days and B in 27 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. How many more days does A need? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 11.33. Use 54 work units. Rates: A = 3, B = 2 units/day. Remaining = 54 − 4×5. Divide by A’s rate 3.

questions.stem: A boat travels 315 km downstream and the same distance upstream. Its still-water speed is 18 km/h and stream speed is 3 km/h. Find the total time (hours).
A invests ₹30000 for 12 months. B invests ₹90000 for 6 months. Total profit is ₹72000. Find B’s share (₹).

questions.stem: What is the difference (₹) between compound interest and simple interest on ₹27000 at 5% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 67.5. For 2 years, CI − SI = P(r/100)² = 27000 × (5/100)².

questions.stem: A vessel contains 45 litres of milk and water in ratio 3:2. How many litres of pure milk must be added to make the ratio 2:1?
questions.explanation: Answer: 9. Milk = 3V/5, water = 2V/5. Solve (3V/5 + x)/(2V/5) = 2; x = V/5 = 9.

questions.stem: The average of 20 numbers is 69. One number, 81, is replaced and the average rises by 4. What is the new number?
questions.explanation: Answer: 161. Total increases by 20 × 4. New number = 81 + 80.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his daughter. After 7 years, their combined age will be 66 years. Find the father’s present age.
questions.explanation: Answer: 39. Let daughter’s age be x. Father is 3x. 4x + 14 = 66; x = 13, so father = 39.
